te: Preparing the Chiang Mai–Lampang visit, a seminar on population structure, and studying the home workers protection bill
se: The committee approved the schedule of the field visit to Chiang Mai and Lampang (16–18 Dec 2026), considered the programme of the seminar “Population Structure and Quality of Life: Challenges and Directions of Thai Social Policy in the Next Decade” (12 Nov 2026) and approved the project in honour of the Father of the Land for National Day and National Father's Day 2026 (30 Nov–4 Dec 2026 at Parliament House), which includes the National Outstanding Father Awards. It then studied the draft Home Workers Protection Act (No. ..) under rule 119, which extends protection to commercial, agricultural and service work, sets a minimum age for home workers and bars children and pregnant women from work that may be dangerous, in line with International Labour Organization conventions. It also considered the draft policy proposals of the subcommittee on women on births registered naming a false Thai father, and appointed 1 honorary adviser.

te: Meeting summary video · Preparing the Chiang Mai–Lampang visit, a seminar on population structure, and studying the home workers protection bill
Seminar programme on population structure approved, and honorary advisers appointed
se: The meeting considered the draft programme of the committee's overall seminar “Population Structure and Quality of Life: Challenges and Directions of Thai Social Policy in the Next Decade” on Thursday 12 November 2026, which links the work of all 3 subcommittees in 4 breakout groups: supporting healthy births and growth; strong families and women's employment; technology and innovation for older persons; and local communities and quality of life. The meeting approved it in principle and asked the secretariat to coordinate the participants of each breakout room. It then noted progress reports from committee members serving on ad hoc committees considering 3 bills, and resolved to appoint 3 honorary advisers to the committee from 29 October 2026.

te: Meeting summary video · Seminar programme on population structure approved, and honorary advisers appointed
False birth registrations: hearing Foreign Affairs, Digital Economy and Society, and Immigration
se: The committee continued to follow births registered with a false father, inviting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, the Immigration Bureau and the association of village and sub-district heads of Thailand to look at gaps in the system and data links between agencies. The results will be used for policy proposals and ways to improve the law that keep the grant of Thai nationality accurate while protecting children's rights in balance. The committee also set its way of working for 2027, including a seminar and field visits to Chiang Mai and Lampang (Nov–Dec 2026), appointed 1 academic and 2 honorary advisers, and appointed subcommittee members and advisers.

False birth registrations: hearing the Medical Council and royal colleges, and studying the maritime labour bill
se: The committee followed births registered with a false father, inviting the Medical Council, the Royal Thai College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, the Royal College of Pediatricians of Thailand and the Thailand Nursing and Midwifery Council. The representatives said that staff at health facilities usually cannot know the facts when the documents are complete. They proposed steps before a birth is certified: for example, when one parent is a foreigner and Thai nationality is requested for the child, a DNA test result from a state-approved hospital should be shown, paid for by the applicant, with an electronic system to check DNA results with hospitals to prevent forged documents. The committee also studied the draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..) under rule 119, which it sees as important for protecting the rights and welfare of seafarers, and prepared its way of working for 2027, such as a seminar on promoting births and quality growth.

te: Meeting summary video · False birth registrations: hearing the Medical Council and royal colleges, and studying the maritime labour bill
Setting the way of working for 2027, and changes to positions in the committee
se: The committee set its way of working for 2027: field visits to follow state social policies and projects, studying social problems that affect people, receiving complaints and following them up, seminars to hear views, honouring model persons and organisations, exchanges with agencies in Thailand and abroad, following up its proposals with a database of its work, and policy proposals, with a stress on proactive work and participation of all sectors. It then considered the members of the committee, changing the position of 3 members to “committee member and adviser”, and the members of the subcommittees.

te: Results of the Kanchanaburi visit: a home for older persons and a children's village school
se: The committee summed up the visit to Kanchanaburi (17–18 Sep 2026), which followed care for older persons' quality of life at the Chaloem Ratchakumari Home for the Elderly (under the patronage of Luang Pho Lamyai) and the care of children and youth at the Children's Village School. It then appointed advisers, experts, academics and secretaries of the committee for fiscal year 2027 (from 1 Oct 2026), 1 honorary adviser and 1 adviser of the subcommittee on children.

te: Kratom drinks mixed with other substances: hearing Bangkok and the Department of Local Administration
se: The committee heard the Health Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and the Department of Local Administration on enforcing the Kratom Plant Act B.E. 2022 (2022). Local officials are not yet competent officials under this law, so they cannot make arrests or settle fines themselves, and there is a lack of staff, budget for substance testing and a database of shops. The committee suggested considering changes to the law to give local government more power, supporting the testing budget, assessing the 1,000-metre rule around schools, mapping shops and risk areas, involving schools, communities, village health volunteers and children and youth councils in watching out, and providing treatment and rehabilitation with job training. These will be gathered into policy proposals to the government.
tge: kratom drinks mixed with other substances
it: Cooperation in enforcing the law to prevent the use of kratom drinks (Bangkok and the Department of Local Administration)

te: Kratom mixed with cough syrup: hearing the Narcotics Control Board, the Department of Medical Services and the FDA
se: The committee heard information on the spread of boiled kratom drinks mixed with cough syrup among young people and workers. People entering treatment rose from 988 in 2022 to more than 4,000 in the first 10 months of 2026. Current measures include a ban on sales within 1,000 metres of schools, a ban on street selling and monitoring of online sales, but there are limits, such as low fines and seized goods that cannot be destroyed at once. The Department of Medical Services said the danger comes from the sedatives in cough syrup, which can cause sudden kidney failure in children and teenagers, and warned against people using methadone on their own. The Food and Drug Administration explained how it controls products containing kratom and its measures to stop cough syrup being misused.

te: Early childhood report goes to the Senate, a study on low birth rates, and results of the older persons visit to Pathum Thani
se: The committee noted that the subcommittee on children presented its report on promoting the role of local government in early childhood development to the Senate on 1 Sep 2026 and has begun studying how to respond to a population with few births, with state agencies, universities and international organisations. The subcommittee on older persons held the forum “Volunteers Bringing Children to School” on education for children with disabilities. On kratom drinks mixed with other substances, the committee agreed to invite the Office of the Narcotics Control Board, the Ministry of Public Health and the Food and Drug Administration. It also summed up the visit to Pathum Thani (26 Aug 2026) on care systems for older persons, appointed honorary advisers and prepared the National Outstanding Father Awards.

te: Preparing the National Outstanding Father Awards 2026
se: The committee considered holding the National Outstanding Father Awards 2026 with the Confederation of Health and Elderly Care Establishments Association and the Sanya Dharmasakti Institute for Democracy, to honour and remember the King's grace and to recognise good examples in the role of a father. Activities include a forum, an award ceremony, an exhibition in honour of the King and OTOP product sales. The award ceremony is on Friday 4 December 2026 at Parliament House. There are 5 categories with 9 awardees each, 45 in all; a joint working group will choose them and propose them to the committee for approval.
it: National Outstanding Father Awards 2026 (ceremony 4 Dec 2026)

te: Care of children involved in false birth registrations, with the Department of Children and Youth
se: The committee invited the Department of Children and Youth to give information. There are 77 reception centres (children and family shelters) and welfare homes for long-term care; in 2026 there are 8,198 Thai children and 408 foreign children in care. Children involved in births registered with a false father are protected under the Child Protection Act B.E. 2003 (2003) with multidisciplinary teams while the steps to revoke nationality are completed before they return to their home country. The department suggested making the birth registration process stricter, starting from antenatal care. The committee also appointed honorary advisers and members of the subcommittee on older persons, set how to study preventing kratom drinks mixed with other substances, and prepared 2 field visits, including Pathum Thani (26 Aug 2026).

te: More on births registered falsely, with the health ministry and police, and the volunteer awards
se: The committee continued to follow births registered with a false father, inviting the Department of Health Service Support, the Royal Thai Police and the Immigration Bureau. The Department of Health Service Support explained that it has the power to check standards and medical records of private health facilities, has inspected more than 10 facilities with the police and the provincial administration, and proposed that facilities check the father's details before issuing a birth certificate. The police reported that the cases are under investigation before being sent to public prosecutors. The committee also appointed 5 honorary advisers and advisers of the subcommittee on women, and reviewed the award ceremony “Senate Volunteer Role Models Who Create Value and Inspire Society” (18 Aug 2026).
